title: 90-day integrated focus week plan + exec asks (draft)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working draft for the next 90-day window with two goals: (1) align leadership on a compact set of company-level outcomes we push hard on over the next quarter, and (2) surface the concrete asks we will take to exec/all-hands for approvals, headcount, and runway tradeoffs.

High-level cadence idea:
- Week 0 (prep): Leadership pre-reads + GTM/customer signals snapshot (deliverables: 1-pager for exec).
- Week 1 (focus week): Cross-functional workshops to translate outcomes into project bundles and owners. Visible artifacts: commitment board, risk register, staffing delta sheet.
- Weeks 2–11: Execution sprints, weekly leadership checkpoints (30m) + biweekly deep dives for top 3 projects.
- Week 12: Retrospective, metrics synthesis, and next-window framing.

Draft company priority outcomes (candidate list — pick top 3):
A. Improve inference economics for enterprise customers by 20% unit cost on average for our top 5 workloads.
  - Why: customers cite cost variability as blocker for adoption of Dedicated/Private.
  - How we measure: per-token cost delta (baseline = Jan 2026), adoption rate of recommended quantization profiles, Dedicated capacity utilization growth.

B. SLAs and reliability: reduce p95 tail latency for 2s SLO models by 30% and eliminate two largest incident classes.
  - Why: improve platform trust for mission-critical customers and reduce support overhead.
  - Key signals: p95 latency, incident count, Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR).

C. Close three Private deployments in pipeline (compliance-regulated customers) to hit ARR targets and validate on-prem packaging.
  - Why: revenue diversification and strategic footprint in regulated industries.
  - Key signals: signed contracts, deployment runbook completeness, partner enablement readiness.

D. Developer velocity & adoption: reduce time-to-first-call for new engineers and customers to <30 minutes for hosted API onboarding.
  - Why: accelerates PLG motion and reduces support load.
  - Signals: docs completion %, onboarding funnel conversion, community/OSS contribution growth.

Proposed top-3 (pick one canonical set for exec ask):
- Option 1 (growth-oriented): A, C, D
- Option 2 (stability-first): B, A, D
- Recommended by product/eng workshop: Option 2 (stability-first) — argues we need lower risk and tighter SLOs before scaling adoption.

Concrete exec asks (what we need from leadership this cycle):
1) Headcount: +6 FTEs (all bands) to cover shortfalls: 2 infra-engineering (runtime optimizations), 1 SRE, 1 product manager (private deployments), 1 solutions engineer (enterprise onboarding), 1 program manager (execution & metrics).
  - Rationale: to meet outcome A & B simultaneously without cannibalizing Dedicated support.
  - Cost estimate: ~$1.1M fully-burdened for 12 months.

2) Dedicated investment: $450k one-time for capacity expansion in EU region (burst capacity, hardware reservation).
  - Rationale: reduce cold-start failure modes and support SLA-backed Dedicated commitments.

3) Go/no-go for pilot on two model quantization toolchains (internal experiment) + allocation of lab cluster time (3 weeks per model family).

4) Approve pilot customer list for Private offering (3 named accounts) and permission to start compliance scoping with their security teams.

All-hands run-of-show (draft):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome + norms (CEO)
- 0:05–0:12 — State of the product (CTO): top metrics (latency, costs, capacity utilization, NPS)
- 0:12–0:20 — Customer spotlight (Solutions lead): quick case study on Dedicated customer success
- 0:20–0:35 — Our 90-day focus + asks (Aisha): explain chosen Option, headcount asks, and immediate impacts
- 0:35–0:45 — Breakout prompts (team-level): 3 discussion questions, collect top 3 risks per team
- 0:45–0:55 — Leadership Q&A (live chat + curated questions)
- 0:55–1:00 — Closing + next steps (People Ops): what to expect re: hiring timeline and town syncs

Risks & open questions (working list):
- Hiring pipeline: can we close 6 hires within 90 days? (recruiting forecast attached in linked artifact).
- Tradeoffs: pulling infra engineers into stability work may delay feature roadmap — propose temporary reallocation with targeted scope.
- Capacity spending: one-off EU capacity costs reduce cash runway unless offset by Dedicated commitments. Need FC analysis before final signoff (finance: @Roberto).

Measurement plan (what we will track weekly):
- Leading indicators: PR merge velocity for runtime optimizations, number of onboarding sessions completed, Dedicated capacity utilization trends.
- Outcome indicators: per-token unit cost, p95 latency for targeted workloads, signed Private contracts.
- Reporting cadence: weekly leadership snapshot (1 page), biweekly deep-dive dashboards (Console export).

Immediate next actions (owners & dates):
- Leadership pre-read (Aisha) — due 2026-03-17: short 2-pager and metric appendix.
- Finance model update (Roberto) — due 2026-03-19: run three scenarios showing runway impact.
- Recruiting kickoff for top roles (Priya) — due 2026-03-15: job specs + timeline.
- Technical feasibility spike for quantization pilots (Marco/Evelyn) — due 2026-03-25: cost/benefit memo + lab schedule.
- All-hands logistics (People Ops) — due 2026-03-22: venue, AV, breakout structure.

Notes for discussion at prep workshop:
- How do we weight stability vs growth for next quarter? (voting poll in workshop)
- What is a minimally viable headcount profile to keep roadmap momentum?
- Quick wins: short list of 3 platform fixes that move p95 by measurable amount this quarter.

Appendix (links and quick data):
- Baseline metrics snapshot (Jan 2026): hosted API tokens/month = 18B; Dedicated utilization (top 10) = 63%; average per-token cost estimate = $0.0008.
- Reference tickets: PLAT-1283 (runtime batching improvements), SRE-221 (incident postmortem on region failover).
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/321 (initial batching prototype).

Tone: this is a working document — expect things to move after cross-functional workshop. Mark sections as accepted or rejected in the workshop notes.

Questions for reviewers:
- Do we agree with Option 2 (stability-first) as the canonical ask to exec?
- Is headcount ask defensible vs pulling scope?
- Any missing top risks or customers we should include in pilot?
